```{r}
# Pie chart: proportion of papers across sections 3.2-3.6
pie_plot <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Category)) %>%
  dplyr::count(Category) %>%
  mutate(
    pct   = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1),
    label = paste0(pct, "%"),
    Category = factor(Category, levels = cat_levels)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = n, fill = Category)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1, color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = label),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    size = 4,
    color = "white"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cat_colors) +
  labs(
    title = NULL,
    fill = "Omics category"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title   = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

pie_plot
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "pie.pdf"), pie_plot, width = 8, height = 6)
```


```{r}
# Yearly publication trends by section
plot_data <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Category), !is.na(Year)) %>%
  mutate(Omics = factor(Category, levels = cat_levels)) %>%
  dplyr::count(Omics, Year)

trend_plot <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Year, y = n, color = Omics, group = Omics)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.0) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cat_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(min(plot_data$Year), max(plot_data$Year), by = 1)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, max(plot_data$n) + 1),
    breaks = seq(0, max(plot_data$n) + 1, by = 1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = NULL,
    x = "Publication year",
    y = "Number of included studies",
    color = "Omics category"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title  = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 13),
    axis.title  = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )

trend_plot
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "trend.pdf"), trend_plot, width = 9, height = 6)
```


```{r}
# NOS bar graph: quality assessment of included observational studies
nos_data <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(NOS)) %>%
  dplyr::count(NOS)

nos_plot <- ggplot(nos_data, aes(x = factor(NOS), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#3B5BA5", width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.4, size = 4) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, max(nos_data$n) + 5),
    breaks = seq(0, max(nos_data$n) + 5, by = 5),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = NULL,
    x = "NOS score",
    y = "Number of included studies"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title  = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 13),
    axis.title  = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    axis.text   = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank()
  )

nos_plot
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, "NOS.pdf"), nos_plot, width = 8, height = 6)
```
